Thus three snapshots are generically locally nonidentifying for \(p\ge3\), whereas four snapshots generically identify \(V\) and the full explanation whenever the unique recovered candidate passes the admissibility filters.
body.justification: The theorem isolates the extra snapshot as an identification resource created specifically by unknown common measurement covariance.
body.gap: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 and WangEtAl2024 obtain three-time-point identification when the relevant state covariances are available; their conclusions do not survive the shared unknown additive covariance, while QWENDY2025 assumes supplied covariance matrices satisfy homogeneous congruences.
body.consumer: Experimental designers obtain a sharp reason to collect a fourth destructive snapshot when a common covariance calibration sample is unavailable.
